summary: The old 180-second blocker is fixed and the new structured schema/helper passes review, but unconditional worker-library approval is withheld for a newly demonstrated, pre-existing Jansson allocation-failure path that returns a request containing malformed input JSON.

logic_errors.title: Transient Jansson serialization allocation failure can silently corrupt the evidence payload instead of rejecting the job
logic_errors.detail: In the existing dev image (Jansson 2.14), failing only Jansson allocation 23 or 24 of a one-evidence request_body call makes json_dumps(input, JSON_COMPACT) return non-NULL malformed JSON. The NULL check passes, the malformed text is embedded as messages[1].content in an otherwise valid outer request, and perform has no further request validation before configuring the POST. This is not a leak and is not introduced by structured_output: it reproduces at the same allocation indices on 11d7b6e. The new response_format itself remains correct. The unchanged local response validator cannot establish that the model received the original uncorrupted evidence payload.
logic_errors.reproduction: Compile the embedded request probe with the reviewed interpreter.c under ASan/UBSan. json_set_alloc_funcs injects a single failed allocation, then resumes allocating normally; source-local free calls are routed to the tracked free function for accurate accounting. request_body returns non-NULL at sites 23 and 24; independent Python parsing rejects both inner payloads. The request probe deliberately prints anomalies and exits 0 after allocation-accounting checks; that exit is NOT a request-integrity pass. A separate equality-asserting run exited 134 on the first corrupt result.
logic_errors.required_change: Make request serialization fail closed when the resulting inner input differs from the constructed input or is invalid; similarly protect the final request serialization. A checked serialization path or parse-and-equality verification before transport is one possible bounded fix. Preserve schema, prompt, token/deadline settings and strict validator semantics. Add transient (not only persistent) allocation-failure regression coverage.
logic_errors.verification_required: For each injected Jansson allocation failure, request construction must either return NULL or return a complete request semantically identical to the non-failing request, including the inner user JSON. Retain zero leaked allocations and rerun normal/sanitizer loopback suites.

suggestions.detail: Keep systematic Jansson fault injection in repository tests; happy-path ASan/UBSan tests do not establish allocation-failure integrity.

resolved_findings.evidence: 180000 accepted; 180001 and 0 rejected in executed C driver; active cancellation and shutdown with 180000ms deadline meet <500ms assertions and Python requires a captured HTTP request. Caller integration remains outside this review.

scope.boundary: Standalone asynchronous advisory worker library; not actual router configuration, parent integration, quality, price or deterministic policy integration.
not_claimed: Live GLM requests or model quality/latency
ThreadSanitizer or all libcurl/system allocation failures
scope.caller_contract: Serialized owner APIs, libcurl global initialization, authorized exact scope/evidence/private endpoint, stale-publication rejection, sensitivity preservation and final deterministic policy remain caller responsibilities. Explicit deadline_ms=180000 and structured_output=true must be supplied by integration.

inspection_findings.schema: Exact eight properties/required entries, full reference enums, trajectory.v1, canonical revision, evidence-ID enum, minItems=1/maxItems=16, additionalProperties=false, strict=true. No $ref. Matches MAIN make_request(..., structured=True), intentionally without uniqueItems; local validator still rejects repeated references.
inspection_findings.ownership: Uppercase O json_pack references are incremented before container ownership; local properties/required/refs references are released at the single exit; _new APIs consume transferred values on failures. Helper probes demonstrate zero outstanding allocations at every injected site.
inspection_findings.unchanged: Validator prefix and system instruction compared byte-for-byte with 11d7b6e. Diff adds no reasoning settings, expected-label fields, tools, credentials, routing/scoring authority or parser relaxation. Cancellation epoch and 20ms polling unchanged.

verification.environment: Existing recursant-v4-dev:local image 2b5edaf312e5, docker --pull never --network none --user 1000:1000; source mounted :ro; builds in container /tmp. No installs, pulls or external inference/network.

helper_probe.result: Every injected helper failure returned NULL; zero live allocations. Invalid UTF-8 evidence ID rejected with clean teardown. ASan/UBSan/LSan no diagnostics.

verification.schema_probe: Actual C output with sixteen escaped evidence IDs and UINT64_MAX revision parsed with duplicate-rejecting parser and compared directly to imported MAIN make_request; response_format equal, required set exact/unique, no $ref; structured=false output identical to true output minus response_format.

request_probe.allocation_accounting: Zero live allocations after each call; no ASan/UBSan/LSan diagnostics in diagnostic run.
request_probe.integrity: FAILED: two transient failures yield malformed inner JSON rather than NULL.
request_probe.baseline: Same two transient failures reproduced against 11d7b6e; baseline has 67 allocation sites.

reproduction_artifacts.baseline_reproduction: Use git show 11d7b6e:<path> to create a temporary snapshot of interpreter.c, interpreter.h and context.h; remove .structured_output=true from the probe initializer; mount the snapshot as /src:ro and use the same compiler command.
